extracted.intended_audience: mathematics researchers (authors/readers), librarians, and subscribing institutions
extracted.subtask_description: Information and policy summary for publishing, accessing, and subscribing to American Mathematical Society (AMS) journals, including author tools, access options, archiving, indexing, and usage/statistics practices. Useful for prospective authors, subscribers, and institutional librarians.

rubrics_metrics.name: Peer-review and quality
rubrics_metrics.description: The AMS has published peer-reviewed journals of the highest quality in mathematical research for over 100 years.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each journal is managed by editors who are prominent in their fields; the expectation is peer-reviewed, high-quality research articles, book reviews, and reports appropriate to each journal's mission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Electronic availability and searchability
rubrics_metrics.description: AMS offers searchable electronic versions of its journals; subscribers can search, browse, and print articles specifically in their discipline.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Electronic versions include clickable references and mathematical symbols online; features include expanded search options and easy browsing by recent articles, issues, and tables of contents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rapid electronic publication
rubrics_metrics.description: Articles are published electronically soon after author proofs are returned, so electronic versions are available prior to the print version.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This implies authors can expect online availability before print; subscribers may enroll to be notified by email when articles are electronically published.

rubrics_metrics.name: Linking with MathSciNet
rubrics_metrics.description: Subscribers to both MathSciNet and AMS Electronic Journals can link from reviews to original articles published by the AMS and other publishers and from AMS electronic journal references to MathSciNet reviews.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Article abstract pages provide links to MathSciNet reviews; this bidirectional linking improves discoverability and citation navigation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Free access for print subscribers (license activation)
rubrics_metrics.description: The electronic versions of most AMS and AMS-distributed journals are free to print subscribers. Complete and return the appropriate license agreement to activate your free access today.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A current journal subscription also includes free online access to article PDFs in all volumes of the journal published within the last five years; activation requires returning the license agreement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Perpetual access for subscribers
rubrics_metrics.description: As of 2014, subscribers to AMS journals will maintain perpetual access to subscribed content.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Perpetual access is a subscriber benefit—ensure institutional subscriptions and license agreements reflect this entitlement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Free digital archive (back issues)
rubrics_metrics.description: The AMS has established a complete digital archive of its mathematical research journals. Over 34,000 articles are available from over 100 years of research. All back issues starting with each journal's inaugural issue through 2009 are now freely available in electronic format.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The archive includes multiple major journals (Journal of the AMS, Mathematics of Computation, Proceedings, Transactions, Bulletin); this provides free historical access up to 2009.

rubrics_metrics.name: Indexing and discovery service availability
rubrics_metrics.description: AMS electronic journals are accessible through EBSCO Online, SwetsWise Online, KESLI, CNKI, and CEPIEC's Content Service Platform in China. AMS journals are also indexed in Google Scholar and fully searchable via EBSCO Discovery Service, Ex Libris Primo, and Summon Discovery Service.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Being indexed in major aggregators and discovery services increases discoverability for institutional users and researchers worldwide.

rubrics_metrics.name: Author tools: manuscript tracking and citation services
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors can use a Secure Manuscript Tracking System to check on the status of their papers in the production process. Authors may also use the citation service, through which an author of an article in an AMS ejournal can add bibliographic information about other articles that cite his or her own article.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These tools let authors monitor production progress and augment citation metadata for their articles.

rubrics_metrics.name: AMS Author packages and TeX support
rubrics_metrics.description: AMS Author packages with various TeX options are downloadable in a single Zip file.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors preparing submissions in TeX/LaTeX should use the provided AMS packages to conform to journal formatting requirements and streamline production.

rubrics_metrics.name: MR Lookup reference tool
rubrics_metrics.description: The AMS offers a free reference tool for linking - MR Lookup. Authors can access the MR Database to verify and create references that can link to reviews and original sources. Input basic reference data in MR Lookup and (MR) will deliver electronic publication-ready references with live links to reviews in MathSciNet and to original articles.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use MR Lookup to generate publication-ready references with live links, improving reference quality and linkability in articles.

rubrics_metrics.name: Free access to article references on abstracts
rubrics_metrics.description: Everyone has free access to article References that include links to MathSciNet reviews. The references are found on article Abstract pages.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: References on abstract pages are publicly viewable even when full articles require subscription, aiding discoverability and verification.

rubrics_metrics.name: E-mail notification options
rubrics_metrics.description: A free service allows anyone to receive weekly notification of new articles meeting specified criteria. Messages list journal name, subject area(s), author(s), and article title and contain hyperlinks to the table of contents, abstracts, and the article itself (for subscribers).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notifications can be tailored by journal, MSC subject area, combinations of journals/subject areas, or by issue/article to suit researcher interests.

rubrics_metrics.name: Usage statistics (COUNTER) compliance
rubrics_metrics.description: The AMS is providing usage statistics to subscribers according to COUNTER standards. This initiative facilitates the recording and reporting of online usage statistics in a consistent and credible manner.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: COUNTER-compliant reports allow institutions to analyze how AMS electronic products are utilized; different reports measure usage for journals, books, and MathSciNet.

rubrics_metrics.name: Guaranteed archiving and preservation
rubrics_metrics.description: The AMS guarantees to maintain an electronic archive in perpetuity. An escrow fund has been set up for the purpose of ensuring that files will be converted to readable electronic formats. Back volumes five years prior to the current year are being archived on JSTOR; AMS journals are also available in Portico and CLOCKSS.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Archiving in multiple preservation services (JSTOR, Portico, CLOCKSS) and an escrow fund are mechanisms to ensure long-term accessibility and format migration.

rubrics_metrics.name: License agreement required for electronic subscriptions
rubrics_metrics.description: A signed license agreement is required for AMS and AMS-distributed electronic journal subscriptions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Institutions and subscribers must complete appropriate license paperwork to obtain and activate electronic access and related rights (e.g., perpetual access).

rubrics_metrics.name: Subscription options and pricing incentives
rubrics_metrics.description: You'll get lower subscription rates on AMS journals when you choose to receive only the electronic versions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Institutions should compare electronic-only vs. print+electronic rates; specific current rates are available via journal links and subscription pages.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ethical guidelines and journal policies (existence)
rubrics_metrics.description: Quick Links include 'Ethical Guidelines and Journal Policies'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: While the page does not list the policies in full, authors and editors are directed to consult the AMS ethical guidelines and journal policies for standards on authorship, conflicts, and editorial conduct.
